findings.explanation: app, dataSources ('field mappings shipped with UPS SNMP (upsTestResultsSummary)') and detailedImplementation all treat this as an installable package that provides the snmp:ups:selftest sourcetype and extractions. No such Splunkbase add-on exists. SNMP Modular Input (1537) defaults to sourcetype snmp_ta and ships no UPS-MIB field mappings, so the reader has to create the sourcetype and extractions themselves.
findings.quote: Deploy **UPS SNMP (upsTestResultsSummary)** so MIB-derived UPS diagnostics land with the sourcetype aliases referenced below
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the package name with the real path: SNMP Modular Input (1537) or Splunk Connect for SNMP polling UPS-MIB upsTest objects (upsTestResultsSummary .1.3.6.1.2.1.33.1.7.3, upsTestStartTime, upsTestResultsDetail), with a custom sourcetype snmp:ups:selftest and props/transforms that you write to extract the fields and translate the enum.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are generic templates keyed on host, count and span=1h, none of which the SPL uses. They miss the real causes. upsTestResultsSummary returns inProgress(5) while a test runs, noTestsInitiated(6) after a management-card reboot and aborted(4) when an operator cancels a test, and all of these match != "donePass". Because the object holds the last test result, every poll repeats the same failure until the next test.
findings.quote: **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `power` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: Document inProgress, noTestsInitiated (for example after NMC reboot or firmware upgrade) and operator-aborted tests as expected non-failures. Note that untranslated integer values (1 instead of donePass) make every row match, and that repeated polls of one old result should be deduplicated by ups_name and test start time.

findings.explanation: The SPL neither groups by entity nor counts. It lists every event where test_result is not 'passed' or upsTestResultsSummary is not 'donePass', with ups_name, test_type and the two result fields, and it has no threshold.
findings.quote: grouped by `entity`. Outputs `count` each `the scheduled window`; alert when configured threshold.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual output: one row per polled self-test result where the UPS reports anything other than a passed or donePass outcome, showing UPS name, test type and result.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase app 1537, SNMP Modular Input, is built and supported by BaboonBones Ltd, not Splunk.
findings.quote: Splunk SNMP Modular Input (**Splunkbase app ID 1537**)
findings.suggested_fix: Call it 'SNMP Modular Input (BaboonBones, Splunkbase app 1537)'.

findings.explanation: SNMP Modular Input is a Python modular input. The Universal Forwarder does not include a Python runtime, so the input normally runs on a heavy forwarder or another full Splunk instance.
findings.quote: Validate SNMP reachability from the Universal Forwarder tier using timed polls every 300 seconds
findings.suggested_fix: Check the SNMP Modular Input documentation for supported forwarder types and, if confirmed, replace 'Universal Forwarder tier' with 'heavy forwarder'.

findings.explanation: The SPL has no threshold: it returns every non-passing row, so there is nothing to tune as described.
findings.quote: fires whenever failures breach your maintenance thresholds
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the alert fires on any non-passing self-test result, and describe the dedup or throttle on ups_name that stops repeat alerts for the same test.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: upsTestResultsSummary!="donePass" also matches inProgress(5), noTestsInitiated(6) and aborted(4), and matches every event if the enum is ingested as an integer. The object reports the last test result, so each poll re-emits the same failure. Consider filtering to doneWarning or doneError and deduplicating by ups_name plus upsTestStartTime.

summary: The UC correctly anchors on UPS-MIB upsTestResultsSummary, but it names a non-existent 'UPS SNMP (upsTestResultsSummary)' package as the app that ships field mappings and calls SNMP Modular Input a Splunk add-on. Its description and false positives are templated and ignore the real non-failure enum states (inProgress, noTestsInitiated, aborted) that this search will match.
